correctness.rationale: For the four-dimensional complex Lie algebra [e4,e1]=e1, [e4,e2]=-e2, [e4,e3]=e3, solving the defining antiderivation linear equations gives an 8-dimensional space. Necessary tests on e1,e2,e3,e1+e3 constrain the local maps to the displayed ten-dimensional block-triangular space; the casewise antiderivation witnesses for x4 nonzero, x4=0 with x2 nonzero, and x4=x2=0 prove sufficiency for EVERY complex vector, not just a sampled grid. The exact triple commutators [[D0,E12],E21]=E11-E22, [[D0,E12],E23]=E13 and [[D0,E21],E32]=E31 add precisely the three missing dimensions; the resulting 13-dimensional space stabilizes U=span(e1,e2,e3), is a Lie subalgebra and hence triple-closed. Ordinary pairwise brackets generate those same directions. Independent rational symbolic linear-rank/commutator checks yield dimensions 8,10,13,13. This establishes precisely the single four-dimensional example, not a general closure theorem.
